As an Assembly Worker, you build high-tech machines and learn various techniques. Varied work where you can grow significantly. Wie zoeken we? Engineering should be something you genuinely enjoy working with. You find it interesting to discover how individual components come together to form a complete machine, and you work carefully because quality matters in assembly work. You don't need to have seen everything already: technical insight, curiosity, and the ambition to work increasingly independently are just as important. An MBO qualification in mechatronics, mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, or a comparable technical field. Affinity with mechanical and/or mechatronic engineering. You can read and apply technical drawings. You speak Dutch and/or English. Wat bieden wij je? You'll have the opportunity to gain broad knowledge of mechanical engineering here. Working across different assembly departments means you won't spend years doing the same task-instead, you'll work with a variety of machines and techniques. Think mechanical assembly, mechatronics, robots, conveyors, and service work. Throughout, there's a strong focus on your development and clear opportunities for growth. A salary of € 3,057 to € 3,399 gross per month on a full-time basis, depending on relevant experience. 27 vacation days. 13 ADV days. A temporary employment contract with prospects for a permanent position. One-time bonus payment. Tailored training and courses designed to support your technical development. The opportunity to gain experience across different assembly departments and develop a broader skill set within mechanical engineering. Functieomschrijving You'll be working for an international machinery manufacturer in Lichtenvoorde that develops and produces high-quality machines for the food processing industry. On the assembly departments, skilled professionals with different technical backgrounds work together. The work environment is modern and technological, whilethe atmosphere on the shop floor is practical and collegial. As an Assembly Worker, you build mechanical and mechatronic components, modules and ultimately complete machines. It's precisely this variety that makes this job interesting. There are different assembly departments, which means you'll work with a range of techniques. Think of robot assembly, mechanical conveyors and service assembly. You work on smaller components and larger systems, and sometimes you might be doing something different from one project to the next, or even from one day to the next. Assembling mechanical and mechatronic components and modules. Working according to technical drawings and work instructions. Building modules into complete machines. Inspecting, adjusting and testing assembled components. Identifying and reporting technical deviations. Working safely with professional tools and available equipment. Collaborating with experienced technicians and other technical departments. Contributing ideas for improvements within assembly. Would you like to discover many different aspects of machinery manufacturing as an Assembly Worker? Then apply for this vacancy. We'd be happy to tell you more about the different assembly departments and the opportunities to develop yourself technically.
